# Style rules

26 rules distilled from professional rules editors and designer style guides. Apply them to every line of rules text.

| # | Area | Rule | Do | Don't | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Voice | Address the player directly in the active voice | Pay $1 to gain 2 resources. | The player pays $1 to gain 2 resources. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| 2 | Voice | Use passive voice only for universal prohibitions | Mountain tiles cannot be removed from the map. | Players may not remove mountain tiles from the map. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 3 | Person | Pick 2nd or 3rd person and stay consistent within a section | Each player reveals 1 card from their hand. | Mixing 'you move 3 pieces' and 'the player may move fewer'. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 4 | Pronouns | Singular they; 'that player' when 'they' is ambiguous | If a player has no Scientists, that player may not research Technologies. | he / she / (s)he / s/he / he or she / him or her | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 5 | Modals | may = optional; may not = forbidden; cannot = impossible; must = compelled | If the active player cannot play a card, they must draw a card instead. | Using 'should' anywhere in rules text. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 6 | Verbs | gain (unlimited supply) vs take (limited supply or from a player) vs give | At the end of each round, gain $5. | Using 'take' for something from the general supply. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| 7 | Conditions | Trigger/condition first, effect second | If you roll a 5 or higher, draw a card. | Draw a card if you roll a 5 or higher. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 8 | Sentences | One action per sentence; the one-breath test | Choose one area of the Spaceship. In that area, add damage tokens equal to... | A single sentence with a parenthetical list plus a calculation. | [How to Write a Rulebook for Your Board Game – Entro Games](https://entrogames.substack.com/p/how-to-write-a-rulebook-for-your-board-game) |
| 9 | Time words | when (once/predictable) / whenever (repeatable) / if (may never happen) / at (point in time) | Whenever a player draws a card, ... | Using 'when' for something that may never occur. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 10 | Quantifiers | each (individually) vs every / all (as a group) | Each card is scored according to its Infamy stat. | 'Every card scores' when each scores separately. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 11 | Comparatives | less for singular nouns, fewer for plural; greater/less than for numbers, higher/lower for dice | If you roll a 4 or higher... | Mixing 'greater than' and 'higher' for the same comparison type. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 12 | Hierarchy | turn < round < act/season; phases and steps subdivide | Each player's turn consists of a Draw Phase, an Auction Phase and a Building Phase. | Using 'phase' at two different levels in the same game. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 13 | Orientation | Hyphenate face-up / face-down consistently | Shuffle the cards into a face-down deck. | 'Flip the top card of each deck face down under it' (ambiguous). | [BGG blog: Writing Rules – facing up to breaking the rules (Andy Van Zandt)](https://boardgamegeek.com/blog/5877/blogpost/84240/writing-rules-facing-up-to-breaking-the-rules) |
| 14 | Dice | One die type: 'a die'. Multiple sizes: 4d12 notation. Consider 'dice' for both numbers | Roll 4d12 and place each die on a different runway. | Alternating die/dice unpredictably within one book. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 15 | Capitalisation | Capitalise only specific in-game components, actions and values | Gain 5 Gold from the central supply. | Capitalising Every Important-Looking Noun. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 16 | Emphasis | Bold = keywords/headings. Italic = examples, captions, flavour. No underline. No long all-caps | Bold the keyword where it is first defined. | Underlined rules text; ALL CAPS paragraphs. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 17 | Numbers | Digits for game quantities; spell out flavour numbers and sentence-initial numbers | Two dice may be placed on each territory. | '2 dice may be placed...' at the start of a sentence. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| 18 | Lists | Numbered = sequence. Bulleted = unordered options. Periods only on full sentences | 1. Shuffle the deck. 2. Deal 5 cards to each player. | Numbered labels on a diagram (readers misread them as quantities). | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 19 | Punctuation | Serial (Oxford) comma; one space after a period; double quotes | Farmers, Merchants, and Tailors | Two spaces after a period. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| 20 | Parentheses | Short clarifications only — never new rules | Each player may deploy two Infantry Units (but not other types of units). | Parenthetical that introduces a rule found nowhere else. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 21 | Abbreviations | Expand acronyms on first use in the rulebook (and optionally per section) | Energy Production Rate (EPR) | Multiple visually-similar acronyms: CWC vs CWL. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 22 | References | Cite the target of any cross-reference | see Connections, p. 34 | 'See above' / 'as previously mentioned'. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 23 | Flags | Treat 'exception', 'remember' and 'should' as design smells | Remove or redesign the exception. | Shipping a rule whose only home is an exception clause. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| 24 | Naming | A 'mat' belongs to a player; a 'board' is shared | Place your workers on your player mat. | Calling the shared board a mat, or vice versa. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| 25 | Keywords | Choose names that start with different letters, especially for sibling headings | Dockyards / Assembly | Shipyards / Shipbuilding as sibling headings. | [Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)](https://cur.by/styleguide) |
| 26 | Register | Delete filler and condescension | The victory condition is to destroy all other castles. | 'The victory condition is simply to destroy...' | [BGG: Rules Writing 101 (with an example)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1552162/rules-writing-101-example) |
